reason: The cited evidence supports the general REE mechanism and Y2O3 interfacial segregation in a laser-clad HEA, but the specific claim of ~35 nm Y2O3 particles and the quantitative 50% spallation reduction are not directly evidenced in the provided passages.
premises: Trace Y addition (~0.5 at.%) in FeNiCuAl-based HEA forms ~35 nm Y2O3 nanoparticles at the oxide/alloy interface
These Y2O3 nanoparticles anchor the Al2O3 scale and reduce spallation
Laser cladding induces a nanocrystalline structure that promotes protective Al2O3 formation
The reactive element effect (REE) operates in HEAs similarly to conventional alloys
